newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse to list local Islamic finance firm.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse to list local Islamic finance firm.

text.p: The Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) on Wednesday said it has approved a listing request by the International Murabaha Company.
"The Exchange committee has approved a request to list IMC shares. The actual listing will be on December 31," said a KSE official.

The firm, which changed its name from the International Transport Equipment Co earlier in December, trades in transport equipment, finances the purchase of capital goods -- durable and semi-durable -- and leases capital and durable goods. It was established in April 1980.
Murabaha is an Islamic banking method designed to avert interest payments. Islamic banking does not allow interest on lending.

In 1995 the firm made a net profit of 204,000 dinars compared with 320,000 dinars in 1994 and 6.6 million in 1993. Unaudited figures for the first 10 months in 1996 show a net profit of 869,000 dinars.
It has a paid up capital of 11.4 million dinars and 114.5 million issued shares.
Trade on the exchange is restricted to the nationals of the Gulf Cooperation Council which groups Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.
